claim: React 19.2 is the latest stable minor as of July 2026; 19.2.0 shipped 2025-10-01 and the newest patch 19.2.7 shipped 2026-06-01. No React 20.

React 19 shipped Actions: form action/formAction props, useActionState, useFormStatus, useOptimistic, async useTransition, requestFormReset, Server Functions; Actions auto-manage pending, error and optimistic state and auto-reset the form on success.
quote: Pending state: Actions provide a pending state that starts at the beginning of a request and automatically resets when the final state update is committed. ... Passing functions to the action props use Actions by default and reset the form automatically after submission.

claim: React 19.2 (Oct 2025) shipped Activity, useEffectEvent, Performance Tracks, partial pre-rendering and Suspense batching — no new form/Actions APIs.
quote: React 19.2 adds new features like Activity, React Performance Tracks, useEffectEvent, and more.

claim: form action={fn} runs the function in a Transition with FormData; method is forced to POST; uncontrolled fields are reset after the action; progressive enhancement only when a Server Function is passed from a Server Component.
quote: When a function is passed to action or formAction, the HTTP method will be POST regardless of value of the method prop. ... all uncontrolled field elements in the form are automatically reset.

claim: useActionState returns [state, dispatchAction, isPending]; actions are queued sequentially, must run inside a Transition, throwing inside the action cancels queued actions and rethrows to the nearest Error Boundary, and progressive enhancement needs the optional permalink argument.
quote: Multiple dispatchAction calls are queued and executed sequentially ... If reducerAction throws, React: Cancels all queued actions, Rethrows to nearest Error Boundary

claim: useFormStatus only reads the status of a parent <form> and must be called from a component rendered inside that form — it returns nothing useful in the component that renders the form itself.
quote: useFormStatus will not return status information for a <form> rendered in the same component ... must be called from a component that is rendered inside a <form>.

claim: useOptimistic's setter must be called inside an Action/startTransition; the optimistic value automatically reverts to the real value when the Action settles, including on failure.
quote: The optimistic state automatically reverts to the real value when the Action finishes.

claim: Server Functions require an RSC-capable bundler/framework; the underlying bundler APIs do not follow semver and may break between minors.
quote: the underlying APIs used to implement Server Functions in a React Server Components bundler or framework do not follow semver and may break between minors.

claim: CVE-2025-55182 (CVSS 10.0) was an unauthenticated RCE in React's Server Function request deserialization, affecting React 19.0/19.1.0/19.1.1/19.2.0 across Next.js, React Router, Waku, Parcel RSC, @vitejs/plugin-rsc and rwsdk; fixed in 19.0.1/19.1.2/19.2.1.
quote: An attacker could craft a malicious HTTP request to any Server Function endpoint that, when deserialized by React, achieves remote code execution on the server. Apps using React Server Components are vulnerable even if they don't explicitly implement Server Function endpoints.

claim: Next.js 16 (docs v16.2.10, updated 2026-06-23) documents the canonical stack: <form action={serverAction}>, useActionState for validation errors and pending, useFormStatus in a child submit button, useOptimistic, .bind() for extra args, and zod for server-side validation; Object.fromEntries(formData) also leaks $ACTION_-prefixed protocol keys.
quote: To display validation errors or messages, turn the component that defines the <form> into a Client Component and use React useActionState. ... Note that this object will contain extra properties prefixed with $ACTION_.

claim: next/form extends <form> with prefetching and client-side navigation for GET/search forms; with a string action it behaves like a native GET form encoding fields into search params.
quote: The <Form> component extends the HTML <form> element to provide prefetching of loading UI, client-side navigation on submission, and progressive enhancement.

claim: React Router framework mode uses its own <Form>/useFetcher + route action/clientAction rather than React's action prop; RSC and Server Functions remain in the unstable section.
quote: Actions use React Router's own <Form> component ... useFetcher - No navigation, no history entry (ideal for progressive enhancement)

claim: React Router v8 shipped 2026-06-17, is ESM-only, requires Node 22.22+, React 19.2.7+ and Vite 7+; React Server Components support is still unstable and expected to stabilise in a later minor. React Router v6 and Remix v2 are EOL.
quote: Server Components support remains unstable ... we want to be absolutely sure we're happy with the APIs before committing to them.

claim: The strongest argument for progressive enhancement is not JS-disabled users but the pre-hydration window and slow networks.
quote: Everybody has JavaScript disabled until it's loaded. ... While it's easy to think that only 5% of your users have slow connections, the reality is that 100% of your users have slow connections 5% of the time.

claim: TanStack Start server functions are createServerFn({method}).validator(schema).handler(...); the client build replaces bodies with RPC stubs, and the function exposes a .url that can be used as a plain HTML form action for no-JS submission.
quote: The build process replaces server function implementations with RPC stubs in client bundles ... you can use server functions without JavaScript by leveraging the .url property with HTML forms.

claim: TanStack Start hit its v1 Release Candidate on 2025-09-23 with server functions as the core mutation primitive; RSC support was explicitly deferred to a later non-breaking v1.x release.
quote: React Server Components support is in active development and will land as a non-breaking v1.x addition.

claim: TanStack Start reached stable v1.0 in March 2026 and still lacks React Server Components support.
quote: TanStack Start hit v1.0 in March 2026, bringing type-safe routing and server functions to production. ... TanStack Start v1.0 lacks React Server Components support.

claim: @vitejs/plugin-rsc is the framework-agnostic route to Server Functions in a Vite app: it implements the RSC bundler transforms ('use server' hoisting to encrypted endpoints, 'use client' proxies) over the low-level react-server-dom runtime.
quote: The plugin implements RSC bundler features and provides low level RSC runtime (react-server-dom) API without framework-specific abstractions.

claim: The automatic clearing of uncontrolled inputs after a form action — including when the action returns a validation error — was reported as a React 19 regression and closed as not planned; it is intended behaviour.
quote: If the inputs are cleared after submit, the errors would show up under empty inputs, which is not very helpful. ... Closed as not planned.

claim: The idiomatic workaround for the auto-reset is to return the submitted values alongside the errors from the action and feed them back as defaultValue via useActionState's state.
quote: when we submit the form, but it fails due to errors, the form resets ... we will update the useActionState hook to use the contact as the initial values of the data, but then have it update with the data returned from the action.

claim: The react-hook-form community treats React 19 form actions as complementary, not a replacement: isPending does not sync with RHF's isSubmitting, useFormStatus does not cooperate with RHF, and integration requires manual workarounds.
quote: isPending from useActionState doesn't directly sync with RHF's isSubmitting, requiring manual state coordination ... useFormStatus incompatibility with RHF patterns

claim: The practical hybrid is RHF in mode:'onBlur' for client-side field validation plus useActionState + a shared zod schema for the server round-trip; the author reports it as workable but hacky, with stale-formData bugs needing a timestamp field.
quote: I don't need to make react-hook-form work with Next.js form actions! I can use it for client-side error handling and let React 19 and Next.js take care of any server-side validation.

claim: Consensus comparison: React 19's native form APIs suit simple, server-driven forms with few dependencies; RHF remains the choice for heavy client-side validation, dynamic field arrays and render performance in large forms.
quote: Use React 19 form hooks if you want simple forms that work well with server-side actions and need fewer dependencies. Use react-hook-form if your forms need lots of validation, dynamic fields, or complex behavior on the client side.

claim: TanStack Start server functions are RPC, not RSC: a three-way compile produces a server handler, a fetch-based client stub, and an SSR wrapper that bypasses HTTP in-process.
quote: TanStack Start server functions operate on an RPC (Remote Procedure Call) model, not RSC-based.

claim: useFetcher gives a non-navigating submission with its own Form, state (idle/loading/submitting), data and reset — React Router's equivalent of the pending/result model that useActionState provides.
quote: states available on the fetcher (idle/loading/submitting), data returned from actions or loaders, a Form component to render forms, load() method to fetch data, submit() method to submit data
